name: Oxabolone

lead: Oxabolone is an anabolic steroid in the nandrolone family. People who discuss it in muscle-building circles associate it with lean mass gain and a fuller, more muscular physique.

As an anabolic-androgenic steroid it is classed as an androgen receptor agonist, the signalling that drives greater muscle protein synthesis. The parent compound was never sold as a drug, though an injectable ester, oxabolone cipionate, has seen medical use. Almost nothing has been published on it, and no trials of its effects on muscle or appearance were found.

paras: In physique discussions it is treated as one of the lesser-known compounds in the nandrolone class, used within muscle-gain phases alongside heavy training and a calorie surplus. Specific routines are not well documented in published sources.

Oxabolone is on the WADA prohibited list, so it is banned in most major sports. A 1995 case report described mucosal hyperpigmentation associated with it, and no broader safety data have been published. Anabolic steroids as a class are controlled substances in many countries.

angle.text: Oxabolone is a nandrolone-family anabolic steroid that users associate with lean mass gain. The route is anabolic steroid signalling, which drives greater muscle protein synthesis and more muscle mass. Very little has been published on it specifically.

lead: Oxabolone (also called 4-hydroxy-19-nortestosterone) is a synthetic anabolic-androgenic steroid in the nandrolone (19-nortestosterone) group.[1] The parent compound was never marketed as a drug; its cipionate ester, oxabolone cipionate, is the form that has seen medical use, given by intramuscular injection.[1]

It appears on the World Anti-Doping Agency's list of prohibited substances and is therefore banned in most major sports.[1] Published literature on the compound is sparse. No clinical trials of its muscle-building or appearance effects were found; the only indexed human report concerns a skin and mucosal side effect.[2]

paras: Oxabolone is a 19-nortestosterone derivative carrying a hydroxyl group at the 4-position.[1] Related compounds include its 17-alpha-methylated analogue methylhydroxynandrolone and a further methylated derivative, oxymesterone.[1]
Oxabolone is listed among substances prohibited in sport by the World Anti-Doping Agency.[1] Encyclopedic sources describe no mainstream therapeutic use of the parent compound.[1]
A 1995 case report in Acta Dermato-Venereologica described mucosal hyperpigmentation attributed to oxabolone.[2] Beyond this report, no systematic safety data were located.
No studies found. The only human literature identified is the single case report of mucosal hyperpigmentation noted above.[2]
